# GreatCMS

> GreatCMS is a Git-backed CMS for sites that should not depend on one at runtime.
> It manages only the regions of a page you opt in; everything else stays hand-written code.
> Publishing writes files to a repository, and the commit triggers whatever deploy pipeline already existed.
> 
> It is not a framework plugin. The integration surface is a schema file and some JSON: the tooling
> scaffolds Astro, Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit and Eleventy, and any language that reads JSON can consume it.
> If you are an agent wiring a site up to it, read the standard below and write files: there is no
> SDK to install and no runtime to call.

## Docs

- [The GreatCMS Content Standard](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/spec): The file format a site must contain to be managed: schema, content layout, and resolution rules. This document is the product.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/spec.md
- [GreatCMS Overview](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/): What GreatCMS is, what it deliberately does not do, and the design decisions behind it.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/index.md
- [Getting started](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/getting-started): Scaffold a site's configuration, connect it to the studio, publish.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/getting-started.md
- [The command line](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/the-command-line): Scaffold, extend, type, check, and inspect a site from the terminal.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/the-command-line.md
- [The hybrid model](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/the-hybrid-model): Why a region is opt-in, and what happens before anyone edits anything.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/the-hybrid-model.md
- [Publishing](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/publishing): One commit in your working copy, or nothing at all.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/publishing.md
- [Running the studio](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/running-the-studio): One process, one SQLite file, one password. Nothing it manages depends on it.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/running-the-studio.md
- [Self-hosting](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/self-hosting): One server, three containers; an editor publishes and the site is live in seconds.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/self-hosting.md
- [Previewing](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/previewing): Your own dev server renders it. Never the studio.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/previewing.md
- [Forms and submissions](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/forms-and-submissions): The one thing Git cannot hold, collected in one inbox.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/forms-and-submissions.md
- [Accessibility](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/accessibility): What is enforced by the format, and what is enforced by tests.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/accessibility.md
- [Any language](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/any-language): The standard is files. A reader in Python passes the same suite as the one in TypeScript.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/any-language.md
- [For coding agents](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/for-agents): Every surface an agent needs to wire a site up unattended, and the skill that teaches it.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/for-agents.md
- [The examples](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/examples): Six sites on Astro, Next.js, SvelteKit and Nuxt, and a Python reader, each built to prove one thing.
  - Markdown: https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs/examples.md

## Machine-readable entrypoints

- [docs.json](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/docs.json)
- [llms-full.txt](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/llms-full.txt): every document above in one fetch
- [schema.schema.json](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/json-schema/schema.schema.json): JSON Schema for .cms/schema.yaml
- [config.schema.json](https://greatcms.uwe.rw/json-schema/config.schema.json): JSON Schema for .cms/config.yaml

## Agent skill

The repository ships a skill that teaches an agent to add GreatCMS to a site, extend the
content model, read content at build time and check it before committing:

```sh
npx skills add uwenayoallain/thegreatcms@greatcms
```

Inside a managed repository, `greatcms init` leaves a note in AGENTS.md, and
`greatcms describe` prints the content model as one outline to write content against, and
`greatcms check --json` / `greatcms doctor --json` give machine-readable answers.

## Conformance

A reader is correct if it reproduces the fixture site's resolved documents:

```sh
npx @greatcms/conformance fixtures        # path to the fixture site
npx @greatcms/conformance verify ./out    # ./out holds <region-id>.json dumps
```
